title.zh: 卷二十四 志第五: 地理上 上京路 咸平路 東京路 北京路 西京路 中都路
title.en: Volume 24 Treatises 5: Geography 1 - Shangjing Circuit, Xianping Circuit, Dongjing Circuit, Beijing Circuit, Xijing Circuit, Zhongbu Circuit
title.raw: 卷二十四 志第五: 地理上 上京路 咸平路 東京路 北京路 西京路 中都路 Volume 24 Treatises 5: Geography 1 - Shangjing Circuit, Xianping Circuit, Dongjing Circuit, Beijing Circuit, Xijing Circuit, Zhongbu Circuit

sentences.zh: 金之壤地封疆，東極吉裏迷兀的改諸野人之境，北自蒲與路之北三千餘裏，火魯火疃謀克地為邊，右旋入泰州婆盧火所浚界壕而西，經臨潢、金山，跨慶、桓、撫、昌、淨州之北，出天山外，包東勝，接西夏，逾黃河，複西曆葭州及米脂寨，出臨洮府，會州、積石之外，與生羌地相錯。

translations.literal: The Jin realm’s soil and sealed borders: east to the lands of the Gimir, Wudai, and other wild tribes; north from three thousand-odd li north of Puyu Circuit, with the Huolu Huotuan mengke lands as the frontier; turning right into Taizhou’s Boluhuo-dug border trench and west, passing Linhuang and Jinshan, crossing north of Qing, Huan, Fu, Chang, and Jing prefectures, beyond the Tianshan range, enclosing Dongsheng, meeting Western Xia, crossing the Yellow River, again west through Jia Prefecture and Mizhai Stockade, out from Lintao Prefecture, beyond Huizhou and Jishi, interlocking with raw Qiang territory.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin domain’s territory and borders ran east to the Gimir, Wudai, and other wild tribes; north from over three thousand li beyond Puyu Circuit, with the Huolu Huotuan mengke frontier; then west along the border trench Taizhou’s Boluhuo had dug, through Linhuang and Jinshan, north of Qing, Huan, Fu, Chang, and Jing, beyond the Tianshan, enclosing Dongsheng, abutting Western Xia, crossing the Yellow River, west again through Jia and Mizhai, beyond Lintao, Huizhou, and Jishi, mingling with unconquered Qiang lands.

sentences.zh: 複自積石諸山之南左折而東，逾洮州，越鹽川堡，循渭至大散關北，並山入京兆，絡商州，南以唐鄧西南皆四十里，取淮之中流為界，而與宋為表裏。

translations.literal: Again from south of the Jishi mountains turning left east, crossing Taozhou, passing Yanchuan Fort, following the Wei to north of Dasanguan, along the mountains into Jingzhao, linking Shangzhou; south taking forty li southwest of Tang and Deng, the Huai’s midstream as border, facing Song as inner and outer.
translations.idiomatic: From south of the Jishi range it bent east through Taozhou and Yanchuan Fort, followed the Wei to north of Dasanguan, entered Jingzhao along the hills, linked Shangzhou, and on the south took forty li southwest of Tang and Deng and the Huai’s middle reach as the boundary, facing the Song as paired inner and outer realms.

sentences.zh: 襲遼制，建五京，置十四總管府，是為十九路。

translations.literal: Following Liao institutions, they built five capitals and set fourteen grand commissioner prefectures—nineteen circuits in all.
translations.idiomatic: Adopting Liao practice, they established five capitals and fourteen grand commissioner prefectures, making nineteen circuits.

sentences.zh: 其間散府九，節鎮三十六，防禦郡二十二，刺使郡七十三，軍十有六，縣六百三十二。

translations.literal: Among them: nine scattered prefectures, thirty-six military commissioners, twenty-two defense commanderies, seventy-three inspector commanderies, sixteen armies, six hundred thirty-two counties.
translations.idiomatic: Within this lay nine scattered prefectures, thirty-six jiedushi posts, twenty-two defense commanderies, seventy-three cishi commanderies, sixteen armies, and six hundred thirty-two counties.

sentences.zh: 後複盡升軍為州，或升城堡寨鎮為縣，是以金之京府州凡百七十九，縣加於舊五十一，城寨堡關百二十二，鎮四百八十八。

translations.literal: Later they again promoted all armies to prefectures, or promoted castles, stockades, and forts to counties; thus Jin’s capitals, prefectures, and zhou totaled one hundred seventy-nine, counties fifty-one more than before, stockades, forts, and passes one hundred twenty-two, towns four hundred eighty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Later they promoted every army to a prefecture, or elevated castles, stockades, and forts to counties; Jin thus had one hundred seventy-nine capital-prefecture-zhou seats, fifty-one more counties than before, one hundred twenty-two walled posts and passes, and four hundred eighty-eight market towns.

sentences.zh: 雖貞祐、興定危亡之所廢置，既歸大元，或有因之者，故凡可考必盡著之，其所不載則闕之。

translations.literal: Though what the Zhenyou and Xingding peril abolished, once returned to Great Yuan some were kept; therefore whatever can be verified is fully recorded—what is not recorded is left blank.
translations.idiomatic: What the Zhenyou and Xingding crises had abolished was partly retained under the Great Yuan; whatever could be verified is recorded in full, and what cannot is left out.

translations.literal: Shangjing Circuit
translations.idiomatic: Shangjing Circuit

sentences.zh: 上京路，即海古之地，金之舊土也，國言「金」曰「按出虎」，按出虎水源於此，故名金源，建國之號蓋取諸此。

translations.literal: Shangjing Circuit is the Haigu region, Jin’s old homeland; in the national tongue “gold” is Anchuhu—the Anchuhu River rises here, hence the name Jinyuan; the founding dynastic title likely draws from this.
translations.idiomatic: Shangjing Circuit was Haigu, Jin’s ancestral land; in the state language “gold” was Anchuhu, and because the Anchuhu River rose there the place was called Jinyuan—the dynasty’s name likely came from this.

sentences.zh: 國初稱為內地，天眷元年號上京。

translations.literal: At the founding it was called the inner land; in Tianjuan year 1 it was titled Shangjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the founding era it was the inner land; in the first year of Tianjuan it became Shangjing.

sentences.zh: 海陵貞元元年遷都于燕，削上京之號，止稱會寧府，稱為國中者以違制論。

translations.literal: In Hailing’s first Zhenyuan year the capital moved to Yan; the Shangjing title was cut, leaving only Huining Prefecture—calling it “within the state” was punished as a violation.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing moved the capital to Yan in Zhenyuan 1, the Shangjing name was dropped and only Huining Prefecture remained—anyone who called it “the heartland” faced charges of breach.

sentences.zh: 大定十三年七月，後為上京。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the thirteenth year of Dading, it again became Shangjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Dading 13 it was restored as Shangjing.

sentences.zh: 其山有長白、青嶺、馬紀嶺、完都魯，水有按出虎水、混同江、來流河、宋瓦江、鴨子河。

translations.literal: Its mountains: Changbai, Qingling, Majiling, Wandulu; its waters: Anchuhu River, Huntong River, Liuliu River, Songwa River, Yazi River.
translations.idiomatic: Its mountains were Changbai, Qingling, Majiling, and Wandulu; its rivers the Anchuhu, Huntong, Liuliu, Songwa, and Yazi.

sentences.zh: 府一，領節鎮四，防禦一，縣六，鎮一。

translations.literal: One prefecture; four military commissioners, one defense commandery, six counties, one town.
translations.idiomatic: One prefecture; four jiedushi circuits, one defense commandery, six counties, one town.

sentences.zh: 舊有會平州，天會二年築，契丹之周特城也，後廢。

translations.literal: Formerly there was Huiping Prefecture, built in Tianhui 2—Liao’s Zhoute Fort—later abolished.
translations.idiomatic: There had been Huiping Prefecture, built in Tianhui 2 on the site of Liao’s Zhoute Fort, later abolished.

sentences.zh: 其宮室有乾元殿，天會三年建，天眷元年更名皇極殿。

translations.literal: Its palaces had the Qianyuan Hall, built Tianhui 3, renamed Huangji Hall in Tianjuan 1.
translations.idiomatic: Palaces included the Qianyuan Hall, built in Tianhui 3 and renamed Huangji in Tianjuan 1.

sentences.zh: 慶元宮，天會十三年建，殿曰辰居，門曰景暉，天眷二年安太祖以下禦容，為原廟。

translations.literal: Qingyuan Palace, built Tianhui 13, hall Chenju, gate Jinghui; in Tianjuan 2 the imperial portraits from Taizu down were installed as the remote temple.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyuan Palace, built in Tianhui 13 with hall Chenju and gate Jinghui; in Tianjuan 2 portraits from Taizu downward were placed there as the remote ancestral shrine.

sentences.zh: 朝殿，天眷元年建，殿曰敷德，門曰延光，寢殿曰宵衣，書殿曰稽古。

translations.literal: Audience Hall, built Tianjuan 1, hall Fude, gate Yanguang, sleeping hall Xiaoyi, book hall Jigu.
translations.idiomatic: The Audience Hall, built in Tianjuan 1 with hall Fude, gate Yanguang, sleeping hall Xiaoyi, and book hall Jigu.

sentences.zh: 又有時德宮、明德殿，熙宗嘗享太宗禦容于此，太后所居也。

translations.literal: Also Shide Palace and Mingde Hall—Xizong once offered Taizong’s portrait here; the empress dowager’s residence.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Shide Palace and Mingde Hall, where Xizong once honored Taizong’s portrait and where the empress dowager lived.

sentences.zh: 涼殿，皇統二年構，門曰延福，樓曰五雲，殿曰重明。

translations.literal: Cooling Hall, built Huangtong 2, gate Yanfu, tower Wuyun, hall Chongming.
translations.idiomatic: The Cooling Hall, built in Huangtong 2 with gate Yanfu, tower Wuyun, and hall Chongming.

sentences.zh: 東廡南殿曰東華，次曰廣仁。

translations.literal: East wing south hall Donghua, next Guangren.
translations.idiomatic: On the east wing’s south side were Donghua Hall and, next, Guangren.

sentences.zh: 西廡南殿曰西清，次曰明義。

translations.literal: West wing south hall Xiqing, next Mingyi.
translations.idiomatic: On the west wing’s south side were Xiqing Hall and, next, Mingyi.

sentences.zh: 重明後，東殿曰龍壽，西殿曰奎文。

translations.literal: Behind Chongming, east hall Longshou, west hall Kuiwen.
translations.idiomatic: Behind Chongming stood Longshou on the east and Kuiwen on the west.

translations.literal: Seasonal Hall and its gate called Fengyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Seasonal Hall and its gate Fengyuan.

sentences.zh: 有泰和殿，有武德殿，有薰風殿。

translations.literal: There were Taihe, Wude, and Xunfeng halls.
translations.idiomatic: There were the Taihe, Wude, and Xunfeng halls.

sentences.zh: 其行宮有天開殿，爻剌春水之地也。

translations.literal: Travel palaces had the Tiankai Hall, at the Yaola spring-water grounds.
translations.idiomatic: Travel palaces included the Tiankai Hall at the Yaola spring camp.

translations.literal: There was a Huntong River travel palace.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a Huntong River travel palace.

sentences.zh: 太廟、社稷，皇統三年建，正隆二年毀。

translations.literal: Grand Temple and Altar of Soil and Grain, built Huangtong 3, destroyed Zhenglong 2.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Temple and Altar of Soil and Grain, built in Huangtong 3 and razed in Zhenglong 2.

sentences.zh: 原廟，天眷元年以春亭名天元殿，安太祖、太宗、徽宗及諸後禦容。

translations.literal: Remote temple: in Tianjuan 1 the spring pavilion was named Tianyuan Hall and held portraits of Taizu, Taizong, Huizong, and the empresses.
translations.idiomatic: The remote shrine: in Tianjuan 1 the spring pavilion became Tianyuan Hall, housing portraits of Taizu, Taizong, Huizong, and the consorts.

sentences.zh: 春亭者，太祖所嘗禦之所也。

translations.literal: The spring pavilion was where Taizu had once resided.
translations.idiomatic: The spring pavilion was where Taizu had once stayed.

sentences.zh: 天眷二年作原廟，皇統七年改原廟乾文殿曰世德，正隆二年毀。

translations.literal: Tianjuan 2 made the remote temple; Huangtong 7 renamed its Qianwen Hall Shide; Zhenglong 2 destroyed it.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjuan 2 it became the remote temple; in Huangtong 7 the Qianwen Hall was renamed Shide; Zhenglong 2 destroyed it.

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dading Taizu’s temple was rebuilt.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 5 Taizu’s temple was rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 興聖宮，德宗所居也，天德元年名之。

translations.literal: Xingsheng Palace, where Dezong lived, named in Tiande 1.
translations.idiomatic: Xingsheng Palace, Dezong’s residence, named in Tiande 1.

sentences.zh: 興德宮，後更名永祚宮，睿宗所居也，光興宮，世宗所居也。

translations.literal: Xingde Palace, later renamed Yongzuo Palace, where Ruizong lived; Guangxing Palace, where Shizong lived.
translations.idiomatic: Xingde Palace, later Yongzuo, was Ruizong’s home; Guangxing Palace was Shizong’s.

sentences.zh: 正隆二年命吏部郎中蕭彥良盡毀宮殿、宗廟、諸大族邸第及儲慶寺，夷其趾，耕墾之。

translations.literal: In Zhenglong 2 the Ministry Personnel Director Xiao Yanliang was ordered to destroy palaces, ancestral temples, great-clan mansions, and Chuqing Temple, level the sites, and plow them.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenglong 2 Personnel Director Xiao Yanliang was ordered to raze palaces, ancestral shrines, great-family mansions, and Chuqing Temple, level the ground, and farm it.

sentences.zh: 大定二十一年後修宮殿，建城隍廟。

translations.literal: After the twenty-first year of Dading palaces were repaired and a city-god temple built.
translations.idiomatic: After Dading 21 the palaces were repaired and a city-god temple erected.

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year the city was bound with brick.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 the walls were faced with brick.

sentences.zh: 有皇武殿，擊球校射之所也。

translations.literal: There was Huangwu Hall, a place for cuju and archery practice.
translations.idiomatic: There was Huangwu Hall for cuju and archery.

sentences.zh: 有雲錦亭，有臨漪亭，為籠鷹之所，在按出虎水側。

translations.literal: There were Yunjin and Linyi pavilions for hawking, beside the Anchuhu River.
translations.idiomatic: Yunjin and Linyi pavilions for hawking stood beside the Anchuhu.

translations.literal: Huining yi, set at the same time as the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Huining county seat, established with the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 有長白山、青嶺、馬紀嶺、勃野澱、綠野澱。

translations.literal: There were Changbai, Qingling, Majiling, Boye Marsh, and Luye Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: It had Changbai, Qingling, Majiling, Boye Marsh, and Luye Marsh.

sentences.zh: 有按出虎河，又書作阿術滸。

translations.literal: There was the Anchuhu River, also written Ashu Hu.
translations.idiomatic: The Anchuhu River, also written Ashu Hu.

translations.literal: There were the Huntong and Liuliu rivers.
translations.idiomatic: There were the Huntong and Liuliu rivers.

sentences.zh: 有得勝陀，國言忽土皚葛蠻，太祖誓師之地也。

translations.literal: There was Desheng Tuo—in the national tongue Hutu Aige Man—the place where Taizu swore his oath.
translations.idiomatic: Desheng Tuo—Hutu Aige Man in the state tongue—was where Taizu mustered his oath.

sentences.zh: 曲江初名鎮東，大定七年置，十三年更今名。

translations.literal: Qujiang, first named Zhendong, set in the seventh year of Dading, renamed in the thirteenth.
translations.idiomatic: Qujiang, first Zhendong, founded in Dading 7 and renamed in 13.

translations.literal: Yichun, set in the seventh year of Dading.
translations.idiomatic: Yichun, established in Dading 7.

translations.literal: There was the Yazi River.
translations.idiomatic: There was the Yazi River.

translations.literal: Zhaozhou, lower grade, defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozhou, lower grade, with a defense commissioner.

translations.literal: Formerly the Chuhe River post.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Chuhe River market.

sentences.zh: 天會八年，以太祖兵勝遼，肇基王績於此，遂建為州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianhui, because Taizu’s army defeated Liao here and laid the royal foundation, it was made a prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 8, because Taizu’s victory over Liao founded the royal enterprise here, it became a prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天眷元年十月，置防禦使，隸會寧府。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of Tianjuan 1 a defense commissioner was set, subordinate to Huining Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Tianjuan 1 a defense commissioner was appointed, under Huining Prefecture.

translations.literal: In Hailing’s time it was once a sub-prefecture of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hailing it briefly served as a sub-prefecture of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 承安三年，複以為太祖神武隆興之地，升為節鎮，軍名武興。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chengan it again became the land of Taizu’s divine martial rise, promoted to a military commissioner, army name Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: In Chengan 3, as Taizu’s land of divine martial ascent, it was again made a jiedushi post with army name Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 五年，置漕運司，以提舉兼州事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year a transport office was set, the transport intendant also holding prefectural duties.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 a transport office was added, its intendant doubling as prefect.

translations.literal: Later the army was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The army was later abolished.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年複升為武興軍節鎮，置招討司，以使兼州事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou it was again raised to Wuxing Army jiedushi, with a pacification office—the commissioner also holding prefectural duties.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou 2 it was restored as Wuxing Army jiedushi with a pacification office, the commissioner also serving as prefect.

translations.literal: Households five thousand three hundred seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: Households: 5,375.

translations.literal: One county:
translations.idiomatic: One county:

translations.literal: Shixing yi, set when the prefecture was founded.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing county seat, founded with the prefecture.

translations.literal: There were the Yazi River and Heilong River.
translations.idiomatic: It had the Yazi and Heilong rivers.

translations.literal: Longzhou, lower grade, Lishe Army military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Longzhou, lower grade, Lishe Army jiedushi.

sentences.zh: 古扶餘之地，遼太祖時，有黃龍見，遂名黃龍府。

translations.literal: Ancient Fuyu land; in Taizu of Liao’s time a yellow dragon appeared, hence Huanglong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Old Fuyu territory; under Liao Taizu a yellow dragon appeared, so it was named Huanglong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天眷三年，改為濟州，以太祖來攻城時大軍徑涉，不假舟楫之祥也，置利涉軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianjuan it became Jizhou—because when Taizu came to storm the city the great army waded straight across without boats, an auspicious sign—and Lishe Army was set.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjuan 3 it became Jizhou—Taizu’s army had forded without boats when he besieged the city—and Lishe Army was established.

sentences.zh: 天德三年置上京路都轉運司，四年，改為濟州轉運司。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiande the Shangjing Circuit grand transport office was set; in the fourth year it became the Jizhou transport office.
translations.idiomatic: Tiande 3 saw the Shangjing grand transport office; in year 4 it became the Jizhou transport office.

sentences.zh: 大定二十九年嫌與山東路濟州同，更今名。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Dading, because it shared a name with Shandong’s Jizhou, it took the present name.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 29, to avoid confusion with Shandong’s Jizhou, it received its current name.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，升為隆安府，戶一萬一百八十。

translations.literal: At the start of Zhenyou it was raised to Long’an Prefecture; households ten thousand one hundred eighty.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyou it became Long’an Prefecture; households: 10,180.

translations.literal: One county:
translations.idiomatic: One county:

translations.literal: Lishe yi, set when the prefecture was founded.
translations.idiomatic: Lishe county seat, founded with the prefecture.

translations.literal: There were the Huntong and Liuliu rivers.
translations.idiomatic: It had the Huntong and Liuliu rivers.

sentences.zh: 鎮一興縣同時置，有混同館。

translations.literal: One town set with the county; there was the Huntong guesthouse.
translations.idiomatic: One town founded with the county; there was the Huntong guesthouse.

translations.literal: Xinzhou, lower grade, Zhangxin Army inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Xinzhou, lower grade, Zhangxin Army cishi.

sentences.zh: 本渤海懷遠軍，遼開泰七年建，取諸路漢民置。

translations.literal: Originally Bohai Huaiyuan Army; Liao built it in the seventh year of Kaitai, gathering Han subjects from all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Originally Bohai’s Huaiyuan Army; Liao founded it in Kaitai 7 with Han settlers from every circuit.

translations.literal: Households seven thousand three hundred fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Households: 7,359.

translations.literal: One county:
translations.idiomatic: One county:

translations.literal: Wuchang was originally Bohai Huaifu county land.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang was formerly Bohai Huaifu county territory.

translations.literal: One town, eighty households.
translations.idiomatic: One town of eighty households.

sentences.zh: 蒲與路，國初置萬戶，海陵例罷萬戶，乃改置節度使。

translations.literal: Puyu Circuit: at the founding a wanhu was set; by Hailing’s precedent wanhu were abolished and a military commissioner installed.
translations.idiomatic: Puyu Circuit: a wanhu at the founding; under Hailing’s rule wanhu were abolished and a jiedushi appointed.

translations.literal: In the third year of Chengan a deputy military commissioner was set.
translations.idiomatic: In Chengan 3 a deputy jiedushi was added.

sentences.zh: 南至上京六百七十里，東南至胡裏改一千四百里，北至北邊界火魯火疃謀克三千里。

translations.literal: South to Shangjing six hundred seventy li, southeast to Huligai one thousand four hundred li, north to the northern frontier Huolu Huotuan mengke three thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Six hundred seventy li south to Shangjing, one thousand four hundred li southeast to Huligai, three thousand li north to the Huolu Huotuan mengke frontier.

translations.literal: Helan Circuit had a grand commissioner prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Helan Circuit had a grand commissioner prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，改總管為尹，仍兼兵馬都總管。

translations.literal: In the first Zhenyuan year the commissioner became a yin, still also commander of all forces.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 1 the commissioner became a yin, still commanding all troops.

sentences.zh: 承安三年，設兵馬副總管。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chengan a deputy troop commander was set.
translations.idiomatic: In Chengan 3 a deputy troop commander was appointed.

sentences.zh: 舊貢海蔥，大定二十七年罷之。

translations.literal: Former tribute of sea asparagus; abolished in the twenty-seventh year of Dading.
translations.idiomatic: It once sent sea asparagus as tribute, ended in Dading 27.

translations.literal: There was the Yilu River.
translations.idiomatic: There was the Yilu River.

sentences.zh: 西至上京一千八百里，東南至高麗界五百里。

translations.literal: West to Shangjing one thousand eight hundred li, southeast to the Goryeo border five hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: One thousand eight hundred li west to Shangjing, five hundred li southeast to the Goryeo border.

translations.literal: Supin Circuit, military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Supin Circuit, jiedushi.

translations.literal: Under Liao it was Shuaibin Prefecture with an inspector set.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liao it was Shuaibin Prefecture with a cishi.

sentences.zh: 」上令無水草地官為建屋，及臨潢路諸堡皆以放良人戍守。

sentences.zh: 」上以年饑權寢，姑令開壕為備。

sentences.zh: 乃言：「可築二百五十堡，堡日用工三百，計一月可畢，糧亦足備，可為邊防久計，泰州九堡、臨潢五堡之地斥鹵，官可為屋外，自撒裏乃以西十九堡，舊戍軍舍少，可令大鹽濼官木三萬餘，與直東堡近嶺求木，每家官為構室一椽以處之。」

translations.literal: He then said: “Two hundred fifty forts can be built; each fort three hundred workmen per day, estimated one month to finish, grain also sufficient to prepare—this can serve as a long-term border plan. Taizhou’s nine forts and Linfu’s five forts lie on saline-barren ground; officials can build outer houses. From Salinai west the nineteen forts have few old garrison barracks; the Great Salt Marsh office can supply thirty thousand-odd timbers, and timber can be sought from ridges near Zhidong Fort; for each household officials can build one-room dwellings to house them.”
translations.idiomatic: He then proposed 250 forts at 300 laborers per fort per day, finishable in a month with grain in hand—a lasting border scheme. On Taizhou’s nine and Linfu’s five barren sites the state should erect outer shelters; west of Salinai, where the nineteen old forts lacked barracks, thirty thousand logs from the Great Salt Marsh office plus timber from ridges near Zhidong Fort could supply one official-built room per household.
